summary: SDK concurrency + aggressive retry jitter causing 429 quota throttles to appear as inference timeouts for NeuroMed
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NeuroMed, enterprise) reports a spike in perceived inference timeouts starting 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC. Symptoms look like long tail responses or client-side timeouts, but request traces show repeated 429 responses from the API. The NeuroMed SDK is configured with high concurrency and an aggressive retry loop which appears to amplify quota-enforced 429 throttles into a client-visible outage.

Impact:
- Production traffic for NeuroMed's clinical notes summarization endpoint experienced degraded throughput and many user-facing failures for ~3 hours.
- Estimated 18k requests affected, intermittent errors caused background tasks to queue up and retry, increasing latency for other endpoints.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod) - us-east region
- Customer using Redwood JS SDK v1.8.2 with default retry strategy overridden to high concurrency (maxConcurrency=50) and short initial retry delay (50ms).
- Customer pinned to model redwood-alpha-3b; fallbacks to open-llama-7b configured.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by NeuroMed / reproduced internally):
1) Customer signature code: fire large batch of concurrent requests (50 concurrent generators) against /v1/generate for 10 minutes.
2) SDK receives 429s from API gateway and immediately retries with exponential backoff starting at 50ms and jitter disabled.
3) Retried requests re-enter the gateway and are counted against the same quota bucket, producing more 429s.
4) Observed: request latencies climb, many client-side timeouts after retries, and streaming connections drop.

Observed behavior:
- Short bursts of 429s at the edge, followed by a retry storm from the SDK producing an amplification loop.
- Traces show repeated 429s for the same original client request id and high retry counts per request.
- On the console, token-level cost looks normal, but per-route throughput drops because retries are queued.

Expected behavior:
- SDK should back off when 429 signals are returned and avoid immediate retriggering that counts toward quota.
- Platform should provide a clearer quota signal to SDKs so retries are coordinated (e.g., Retry-After, or a soft-throttle hint).

Logs / snippets:
- Example gateway log: "2026-03-09T18:07:12Z | req=abc123 | upstream=quota-service | status=429 | reason=quota_exceeded | remaining=0"
- SDK client log (NeuroMed): "sendRequest(id=xyz) -> 429; retrying after 50ms (attempt 1)" repeated 6x.
- Trace link (internal): https://internal.redwood.com/traces/2026-03-09/neuro/abc123

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Lower concurrency to 8 and enable exponential backoff with base 500ms and jitter. Customer reports immediate improvement when reduced.

Notes on customer impact and urgency:
- Customer is enterprise and running nightly jobs that missed processing windows; requires mitigation and guidance ASAP.
steps_to_reproduce: Configure Redwood JS SDK v1.8.2 with maxConcurrency=50 and retryDelayBase=50ms
Send sustained concurrent load (50 parallel requests) to /v1/generate for 10 minutes
Observe repeated 429 responses and client retries inflating request counts
investigation_notes: 03/10 - Initial triage: Support reproduced amplification locally using customer's SDK settings. Observed identical retry counts and 429 loops.
03/11 - Eng (serving-runtime) reviewed gateway logs; quota-service returns hard 429 with remaining=0 but no Retry-After header in existing implementation for this quota type.
03/11 - Hypothesis: Short retry base and disabled jitter -> retry amplification. SDK should honor 429 and backoff more aggressively or respect Retry-After header.
03/12 - Confirmed: reducing concurrency and increasing base backoff eliminates client-visible timeouts; service-side metrics show lower request churn to quota bucket.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Maya Chen (Support): Opened ticket with NeuroMed after they reported production failures. Attached logs and initial reproduction steps.
2026-03-11 | Rafael Ortega (SRE): Reproduced locally; filing follow-up with serving-runtime team to add Retry-After hints for quota responses.
2026-03-11 | Priya Nair (Serving Runtime): Noted that quota-service currently does not emit Retry-After for burst-soft-quota; will evaluate safe delay to recommend to SDKs.
2026-03-12 | NeuroMed (customer): Confirmed temporary workaround reduced failures; requests recommendation for SDK update and platform-side mitigation.
2026-03-13 | Rafael Ortega (SRE): Proposed short-term config change: emit Retry-After (ms) in quota 429s and add server-side token bucket smoothing for enterprise customers. Linked PR created.
current_action_items: SRE: Add Retry-After header for quota 429 responses for prod us-east (target: 03/15) - Rafael
SDK: Publish advisory and patch to default retry strategy (increase base delay, enable jitter) and release v1.8.3 - SDK team
Support: Send mitigation guide to NeuroMed with recommended SDK config and follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-14 - Maya
Eng: Evaluate smoothing algorithm to prevent immediate re-counting of retries against quota buckets (postmortem follow-up)
resolution: In progress. Short-term mitigation: customer applied reduced concurrency + longer backoff and saw improvement. SRE will emit Retry-After header and create smoothing for enterprise quota buckets. SDK team to publish recommended settings and patch release.
